title.narrative: Enabling Large-Scale Ecosystem Restoration in Haiti through the Piloting and Implementation of Payments for Environmental Services Schemes

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Stakeholder Engagement96. Civil Society will play an active role in the project. In Haiti’s context of weak governance and unregulated private sector activity, civil society must speak up and demand the rights of Haitian people. From small community-based organizations (CBOs) to large workers unions, the representations of Haitian civil society are many and diverse. The project will galvanize relevant civil society actors through a tailored communications and outreach strategy, so that the project is inclusive, and all voices are heard. This is especially important for civil society representations of women and marginalized groups. Civil society is therefore a key stakeholder group to be consulted throughout the project. Knowledge management97. We confirm that an approach to Knowledge Management (KM) and Learning has been clearly described during Project Preparation in the Project Description and that these activities have been budgeted and an anticipated timeline for delivery of relevant outputs has been provided. Gender-responsive KM strategies for gender mainstreaming across knowledge products and processes will be considered, including: · Use of male and female material (knowledge product, communication, and public education) developers for the diversity of perspectives and approaches, as well as male and female reviewers of these products. · Use of gender-sensitive language and gender-balanced images (women not presented as victims but as agents of change). · Examining context and content (use gender analysis; use convincing gender arguments based on reliable sources and qualitative and quantitative data including sex-disaggregated data). · Referring to (inter-)national policy framework, policies, strategies, and plans, as applicable and appropriate. Socio-economic Benefits 98. We confirm that the Child Project design has considered socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project and these have been clearly described in the Project Description and will be monitored and reported on during project implementation (at MTR and TER).

To enable large scale restoration of ecosystems of importance in Haiti by addressing policy deficiencies, promoting a PES mechanism tailored to the local context, and piloting community-driven restoration models through an integrated management approach in three priority landscapes
